active_inquiry.goal_connection: Identifying the dominant failure mechanism is necessary to choose an intervention that can raise uninterrupted 2-second hold success toward at least 196 of 200 official episodes; reach-only or shaped-reward progress is not sufficient evidence.
active_inquiry.question: For a reproducible baseline learned policy, which mechanism most limits official complete-hold success: failure to reach a valid posture, settling and residual motion, active endpoint hold regulation, inverse-kinematic branch or joint-limit choice, or target geometry and conditioning?
active_inquiry.rationale: The campaign has no candidate, model role, or behavioral evidence, so official assessment is impossible and no-credible-route closure is unsupported. The physical model predicts coupled reach-to-hold dynamics but does not determine which failure phase dominates. A baseline behavioral decomposition will discriminate those explanations and direct the next scientific action.

request.current_synthesis: The pre-campaign physical model supports a coupled-control interpretation: bounded torque at 50 Hz must first move the damped two-joint system to a valid inverse-kinematic posture and then actively cancel residual joint motion so the endpoint remains inside a 1 cm tolerance for 100 consecutive checks. The hold requirement is the most stringent part of the goal because damping alone does not guarantee endpoint regulation, and branch posture and target geometry can change dynamic authority and boundary margin. These are mechanistic expectations, not campaign evidence.
request.decision_frontier: In goal review, choose one bounded inquiry that most reduces uncertainty about the route to 98% success. The key decision is whether to begin with behavioral failure decomposition of a baseline learned policy across target geometry and hold dynamics, or whether an implementation-level obstacle is already sufficiently evident to justify changing the policy, reward, observations, or training distribution first.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 of 200 official episodes to complete an uninterrupted 2-second hold. The initial scientific direction therefore prioritizes understanding and improving the full reach-to-stabilized-hold behavior, rather than optimizing approach reward or endpoint reach in isolation.

request.description: Train a reproducible PPO baseline with the current observation, reward, target curriculum, and runtime parameters; archive all checkpoint candidates for subsequent complete-hold behavioral measurement.
request.rationale: I1 has no candidate or behavioral evidence. A fresh baseline is the highest-value discriminating action because it establishes whether the current learned-control recipe can reach and sustain the official hold at all, while preserving a reproducible reference for decomposing reach time, uninterrupted hold, residual motion, branch/posture, and target geometry.

request.description: Measure the final T1 baseline candidate on the fixed research evaluation panel and record complete-hold outcomes with reach, first-entry, hold-duration, residual-motion, IK branch/posture, joint-limit, conditioning, interruption, and target-geometry diagnostics.
request.rationale: T1 training success reached 0.97 on its training stream, but that does not establish official-distribution success or identify the limiting mechanism. Evaluating the final checkpoint under the held-out research panel is the most discriminating next action for I1 because it tests complete uninterrupted hold and supplies the behavioral decomposition required to choose an intervention.

request.reason: M1 measured this reproducible baseline at 151 of 160 complete-hold successes (94.375%) on the held-out research panel, making it the strongest evidence-backed candidate currently available while remaining below the human goal.

request.candidates_and_roles: T1:checkpoint-100352 is the best-known candidate, assigned by E4, with 100,352 training steps and 0.97 training-stream success. M1 provides its held-out behavioral evidence at 94.375% (151/160). No working candidate is assigned; no separate retained scientific role is needed.
request.cumulative_resource_use: T1 used one fresh PPO training operation for 100,352 completed steps and archived 20 candidates. M1 used one 160-episode research panel at seeds 4200-4359 with evaluation schema 6. E4 assigned T1:checkpoint-100352 as best-known. No official benchmark assessment has been requested.
request.current_goal_gap: The best-known baseline is 5.625 percentage points below the 98% research target and has no evidence of official-distribution attainment. Its remaining failures are concentrated in a negative-angle, near-joint-limit posture: 6 of 9 failures never entered tolerance and 3 entered for only 1-2 checks, while all 9 had negative minimum joint-limit margins.
request.current_synthesis: T1/M1 resolve I1's dominant baseline mechanism sufficiently for an intervention: failures are not primarily generic residual-motion or active-hold regulation failures. The 9 failures occur at target angles approximately -119 to -151 degrees, all approach or cross a joint limit, and remain on the open IK branch; the three entered episodes lost the hold almost immediately. This supports the actionable hypothesis that the learned open-branch posture lacks joint-limit margin for negative-x targets. It does not yet establish whether explicit posture/limit shaping or a different branch policy is the better remedy, so the next experiment must target posture margin without changing multiple factors.
request.decision_frontier: Run one focused training intervention that makes joint-limit margin and valid posture selection consequential while preserving the complete-hold objective, then compare its candidate against T1 on shared research seeds with the same reach, hold, residual-motion, branch, posture, conditioning, and target-geometry diagnostics. Continue only if negative-angle failures and minimum joint-limit margins improve without sacrificing the rest of the distribution.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 of 200 official episodes to complete an uninterrupted 2-second hold. M1 establishes a reproducible baseline at 151 of 160 complete-hold successes (94.375%) on a held-out research panel, so the campaign is below target and must improve the identified failure mechanism before requesting official assessment.
request.next_direction_or_closure: I1 remains open. Modify the PI-owned learning implementation for a single joint-limit/posture-aware intervention, train a new candidate, and measure it in a paired comparison with T1. Do not close I1 or request official assessment until the intervention is measured against the baseline and the complete-hold success gap is resolved or a credible route is exhausted.

request.description: Train a fresh PPO candidate with a single joint-limit/posture intervention: apply a smooth soft-barrier penalty when the minimum joint-limit margin falls below 20 degrees, while preserving the complete-hold reward and official task semantics.
request.rationale: T1/M1 show that the remaining failures are concentrated on the open branch at negative-angle targets whose learned posture reaches or crosses a joint limit; residual-motion and generic hold regulation are not the dominant mechanism. This focused intervention makes safe joint-limit margin consequential without changing the observation, target curriculum, PPO parameters, or success definition. Compare the resulting candidate against T1 on the shared research panel, requiring improved negative-angle reach and minimum margins without sacrificing the rest of the distribution.

request.description: Run a paired 160-episode research evaluation of T2:checkpoint-100352 and T1:checkpoint-100352 on the shared panel seeds 4200-4359, recording complete-hold success and the existing reach, first-entry, longest-hold, residual-motion, branch, posture, joint-limit, conditioning, interruption, and target-geometry diagnostics.
request.rationale: T2's zero training-stream success and negative final reward show that the soft joint-limit penalty did not produce a successful learning run, but training statistics alone cannot establish whether the intervention changed the diagnosed negative-angle posture mechanism. A paired held-out evaluation against T1 on identical episode seeds is the highest-value next decision: it will determine whether T2 provides any behavioral benefit worth rescuing or whether this intervention should be rejected while preserving T1 as best-known.

request.candidates_and_roles: T1:checkpoint-100352 remains the best-known candidate, assigned by E4, with 100,352 training steps and 0.97 training-stream success; M1 and M2 both measure it at 151/160 (94.375%). T2:checkpoint-100352 is rejected after M2 at 22/160 (13.75%) and is not assigned a working or retained role. No working candidate is assigned and no separate retained scientific role is needed.
request.cumulative_resource_use: T1 used one fresh PPO training operation for 100,352 completed steps and archived 20 candidates. M1 used one 160-episode research panel at seeds 4200-4359. E4 assigned T1 as best-known. T2 used one fresh PPO training operation for 100,352 completed steps and archived 20 candidates. M2 used one paired 160-episode panel at seeds 4200-4359 with evaluator semantics e13235fbfa71. No official benchmark assessment has been requested.
request.current_goal_gap: The best-known candidate remains 5.625 percentage points below the 98% research target, with no official-distribution assessment. T2 achieved only 22 of 160 paired research successes (13.75%) versus 151 of 160 for T1, a -80.625 percentage-point delta and 130 reference wins to 1 candidate win. T2 also had zero training-stream success through 100,352 steps, so it provides no credible route to the target.
request.current_synthesis: T1/M1 identify the remaining baseline failures as concentrated negative-angle, open-branch episodes whose learned posture reaches or crosses a joint limit; they are not primarily generic residual-motion or active-hold regulation failures. T2/M2 decisively reject the tested smooth soft joint-limit penalty as a usable intervention: it destabilized learning and produced broad reach/behavioral degradation, so its result cannot be interpreted as evidence that posture margin is irrelevant. The actionable mechanism remains plausible, but the intervention must be changed to avoid adding a competing dense penalty to the PPO learning signal.
request.decision_frontier: Preserve T1 as the sole best-known candidate and reject T2 for all working or retained roles. Before another experiment, restore the T1 recipe so the failed reward code cannot contaminate the next result. Then test one alternative posture/branch mechanism that changes the learned valid posture without adding another broad per-step penalty, and compare it with T1 on shared seeds using the existing complete-hold and behavioral diagnostics.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 of 200 official episodes to complete an uninterrupted 2-second hold. T1 remains below that threshold at 151 of 160 research episodes (94.375%), and M2 shows that the tested joint-limit reward intervention moved decisively away from the goal rather than improving the diagnosed failures.
request.next_direction_or_closure: I1 remains open because the baseline mechanism is actionable and a credible route remains, but the first intervention failed as a learning recipe. In the next session, restore T1's recorded recipe, then pursue a single branch/posture intervention that preserves the complete-hold objective and can be discriminated by negative-angle reach, first entry, hold duration, branch, and joint-limit margin. Do not request official assessment until a candidate closes the success gap on research evidence.

request.reason: Restore the recorded T1 baseline recipe before the next intervention so the rejected T2 dense joint-limit penalty cannot contaminate subsequent training. T1 remains the best-known reproducible candidate, while the next experiment must change posture or branch selection without adding another broad per-step PPO reward term.

request.description: Train a fresh PPO candidate with branch-feasibility observations: append the normalized minimum joint-limit margin for the open and folded IK solutions while preserving the T1 reward, dynamics, target curriculum, PPO parameters, and complete-hold semantics.
request.rationale: T1/M1 localize the remaining failures to negative-angle open-branch postures that reach or cross a joint limit, while T2/M2 reject adding a dense soft-limit reward penalty because it destabilized learning. The new observation features expose the two candidate postures' feasibility directly, allowing PPO to select a valid branch without changing its learning signal. Compare the final candidate with T1 on shared research seeds using complete-hold success and the existing reach, first-entry, hold-duration, residual-motion, branch, posture, joint-limit, conditioning, interruption, and target-geometry diagnostics.

request.description: Run a paired 160-episode research evaluation of T3:checkpoint-100352 and T1:checkpoint-100352 on shared episode seeds 4200-4359, recording complete-hold success and the existing reach, first-entry, longest-hold, residual-motion, branch, posture, joint-limit, conditioning, interruption, and target-geometry diagnostics.
request.rationale: T3's branch-feasibility observations did not match T1's training-stream success, reaching 0.28 versus 0.97, so it cannot be accepted from learning dynamics alone. A paired held-out evaluation is the discriminating test of whether the observation intervention improves the diagnosed negative-angle joint-limit failures without sacrificing T1's broad performance.
